source_description_en: The paper context is Shinichi Mochizuki, Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV (April 2020), proof of Theorem 1.10, Step (viii), printed/PDF pp. 30–31. The step sums the local procession-normalized upper bounds obtained in Steps (v)–(vii), combines the sum with the arithmetic estimate from Step (iii), and bounds the prime-counting contribution l*_mod·log(s^≤). On p. 31 the latter is at most (4/3)(e*_mod·ℓ + η_prm), regardless of whether e*_mod·ℓ is above or below η_prm. The remaining logarithmic and constant errors are absorbed into this term. The final paragraph then obtains the theorem’s numerical constants using ℓ ≥ 7 and d_mod ≥ 1, in particular the estimates (1 − 12/ℓ²)^(−1) ≤ 2 and (1 − 12/ℓ²)^(−1)(1 + 12d_mod/ℓ) ≤ 1 + 20d_mod/ℓ. The reference implementation extracts this numerical assembly into a separate real-inequality helper. The paper does not state a separately numbered lemma with the helper’s full list of parameters and hypotheses.

source_description_en: The paper context is Mochizuki, IUT IV, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), printed/PDF pp. 46–48. At the end of p. 46 the proof applies Theorem 1.10 and uses the selected-prime estimates to replace its numerical coefficients by bounds involving δ and h = log(q_∀). Page 47 bounds the difference between the q-height away from 2 and the q-height away from both 2 and ℓ, absorbs the bounded contribution at 2 into C_K, and introduces ε_E = (60δ)²h^(−1/2)log(2δh). After arranging ε_E ≤ 1 outside the exceptional set, the first display of p. 48 absorbs the error proportional to h/6 by division by 1 − (2/5)ε_E. The elementary estimates there give the coefficient 1 + ε_E and an additive constant C_K. The paragraph then substitutes the equality with the tripodal different and the lower comparison with the conductor to conclude (C2). The reference implementation packages this final numerical absorption as a separate real-inequality helper. The paper does not give that helper’s complete parameter list as an independently numbered statement.
